newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.8 pct in April on month.
newsitem.headline: Canada monthly GDP rises 0.8 pct in April on month.

text.p: - Canada's real gross domestic product, seasonally adjusted, rose 0.8 percent in April after falling 0.2 percent (revised from 0.3 percent) in March, Statistics Canada said on Monday.
GDP Apr 97 mo chg Mar 97 mo chg
Goods industries 194.00 +1.2 191.74 -0.0
Service industries 284.14 +0.8 281.99 -0.4
Business sector 478.14 +0.9 473.73 -0.3
Note: GDP figures are in billions of dollars, seasonally adjusted at annual rates at factor cost, constant 1986 dollars.
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast a rise of 0.6 percent on average for April.
Despite March's drop, GDP has grown on average a torrid 0.5 percent during the first four months of 1997, compared with a monthly pace of 0.2 percent in 1996.

In April, manufacturers, wholesalers and retailers, all of whom suffered losses in March, accounted for about 60 percent of the gain in production. Financial and related services and the mining sector also contributed significantly to the advance, the federal agency said.
Elsewhere, production rose in all major industry groups except government services and utility services.
Retail sales rose 1.1 percent in April after receding 0.8 percent in March, giving an average monthly rise of 0.7 percent this year. Automotive product sales led the gain in April.
Wholesaling activiity rebounded 1.7 percent, Statscan said, in line with the pace recorded in January and February. Wholesalers of consumer goods enjoyed a good month, it added.

Manufacturing production rose 1.5 percent in April, more than offsetting a 0.7 percent decline in March. Output rose in 18 of the 21 major groups, with a 1.9 percent rise in durable goods accounting for more than 70 percent of the advance.

Output in the mining sector increased 2.1 percent in April after remaining nearly the same in the previous two months. Drilling activity led the advance, moderated by declines in output of crude oil, non-ferrous metals and gold.
Financial and related services rose 0.7 percent after retreating the previous two months.
Community, business and personal services rose 0.4 percent, as did construction.
